text: We evaluated aggressive gradient clipping (clip_norm 0.1) during student fine-tuning in a weak-to-strong setup, with gpt2-small as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student. The weak supervisor reached 0.46 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.77, while the clipped student attained transfer accuracy of 0.61 with a standard error of 0.06. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.47 with a standard error of 0.19, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.51. The measured PGR therefore sits below the baseline, and in any case the difference falls well within two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so these data do not support any claim that the intervention helps or hurts. An important caveat is that num_seeds is 1, meaning the run was not replicated and the reported standard errors rest on a single training trajectory. Further seeds would be needed before drawing directional conclusions about clipping.
